cards.front: Prolapse management is driven by symptom burden, not POP-Q stage; surgery is reserved for those failing [___] measures (PFMT, pessary).
cards.context:
Pelvic organ prolapse is graded by the position of the leading edge relative to the hymen (POP-Q stages 0-IV).

The trap is treating the stage rather than the patient — many women with stage II prolapse (descent within 1 cm of the hymen) are completely asymptomatic.

cards.front: In Rh(D)-negative women, Anti-D is indicated for vaginal bleeding at or after 12 weeks gestation or for any miscarriage requiring surgical/medical intervention; it is not routinely needed for a [___] miscarriage before that threshold.
cards.context:
Sensitising events in early pregnancy: any vaginal bleeding ≥12 weeks, miscarriage requiring intervention (medical/surgical), TOP, ectopic, molar, CVS, abdominal trauma.

Exception: threatened miscarriage <12 weeks generally doesn't need anti-D — low risk of significant fetomaternal haemorrhage at this gestation.

The T1 dose is 250 IU IM (smaller than the 625 IU for T2/T3 events) reflecting smaller fetal blood volume. Only Rh(D)-negative women need anti-D.

cards.front: Bedside features split antepartum haemorrhage: a [___] uterus with painless bleeding suggests a low-segment placenta; a hard/woody uterus with painful bleeding suggests abruption. Speculum + urgent USS go first; digital vaginal exam is deferred until imaging excludes a low-segment implantation.
cards.context:
The two major causes of antepartum haemorrhage have opposing bedside signatures: placenta praevia (painless, soft uterus, often recurrent) versus abruption (painful, tense/woody uterus, fetal distress).

Workup is speculum + urgent USS first — digital vaginal exam is catastrophic if praevia is present and undiagnosed.

cards.front: Neonatal resuscitation adrenaline (HR persistently <60 despite PPV + compressions): [___] mL/kg of 1:10,000 IV via umbilical venous catheter (UVC).
cards.context:
Adrenaline in neonatal resus is reserved for persistent HR <60 despite effective PPV + chest compressions for ≥30 sec.

Ventilation remains the priority — adrenaline without effective ventilation is futile in respiratory-arrest physiology.

Volume expansion (10 mL/kg saline) for hypovolaemia; glucose only if confirmed hypoglycaemia.

cards.front: In placenta accreta spectrum, the deepest subtype — villi penetrate through the serosa and may invade bladder or bowel — is [___].
cards.context:
PAS is abnormal placentation: chorionic villi invade beyond the decidua basalis (deficient over a prior scar), so the placenta cannot separate at delivery.

Depth grades the invasion — accreta attaches to the myometrium, increta invades into it, percreta penetrates through the serosa. See the table and A-I-P mnemonic below.

cards.front: Under the 2025 ADIPS criteria, gestational diabetes (GDM) diagnostic thresholds on 75g OGTT are: fasting ≥[___], 1-hour ≥10.6, or 2-hour ≥9.0 mmol/L.
cards.context:
Even modest maternal hyperglycaemia raises fetal hyperinsulinaemia, macrosomia, neonatal hypoglycaemia, and shoulder dystocia risk.

ADIPS 2025 replaced the 2014 values (5.1 / 10.0 / 8.5); NSW Health notified services in August 2025, so older questions may differ.

cards.front: Neonatal hypoglycaemia: BGL <2.6 mmol/L; at-risk groups (LGA, IDM, SGA, preterm) need BGL check at 1-2 hours; symptomatic → IV [___] 10%.
cards.context:
Neonatal hypoglycaemia (BGL <2.6 mmol/L) is the commonest metabolic problem in newborns.

Screen at-risk infants: BGL at 1-2 h then before feeds for ≥12-24 h.

cards.front: [___] is the first-line treatment for eclamptic seizures (superior to diazepam and phenytoin). Loading dose: 4g IV over 15–20 minutes.
cards.context:
Magnesium sulfate is first-line for eclamptic seizure treatment AND prevention in severe pre-eclampsia.

Mechanism is multifactorial — NMDA antagonism, cerebral vasodilation, neuroprotection — not 'just' an anticonvulsant. Magpie and Collaborative Eclampsia trials showed superiority over diazepam and phenytoin.

Loading dose: 4 g IV over 15-20 minutes, then 1 g/hour for 24 hours post-delivery or last seizure. Watch for toxicity (loss of patellar reflexes first, then respiratory depression) — antidote is IV calcium gluconate.

cards.front: Outpatient pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) empirical antibiotics: ceftriaxone (gonorrhoea) + doxycycline (chlamydia) + [___] (anaerobes).
cards.context:
PID is polymicrobial (Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Chlamydia trachomatis, Mycoplasma genitalium, anaerobes); empirical antibiotics must cover all: ceftriaxone (gonorrhoea) + doxycycline (chlamydia) + metronidazole (anaerobes).

Threshold to treat is deliberately low (CDC): any sexually active woman with pelvic pain + cervical motion tenderness OR uterine tenderness OR adnexal tenderness — start treatment.

Most managed as outpatients (oral, review at 72 h); admit for IV if pregnant, severe, suspected tubo-ovarian abscess, no response to oral, or unable to tolerate oral. Sexual partner notification + treatment essential.

cards.front: APGAR components (each 0-2, total 0-10): Appearance (colour), Pulse, [___] (reflex), Activity (tone), Respiration. Assessed at 1 minutes after birth and again at 5 minutes.
cards.context:
APGAR is a 5-component bedside assessment at 1 and 5 min (and q5min if low).

It documents the infant's condition and response to resuscitation — it does NOT trigger resuscitation, which is guided by breathing, heart rate and tone assessed within seconds of birth (AAP/ACOG).

The ranges (7-10 vigorous, 4-6 moderately depressed, 0-3 severely depressed) describe status, not a resuscitation recipe.

cards.front: Emergency contraception: levonorgestrel (LNG, up to 72h), ulipristal (up to 120h), copper IUD (most effective, up to [___] days). LNG is less effective if BMI >26.
cards.context:
Three EC options with different efficacy and time windows: LNG 1.5 mg PO up to 72 h after UPSI (less effective if BMI >26).

Ulipristal 30 mg PO up to 120 h (more effective than LNG in the 72-120 h window); copper IUD most effective, up to 5 days.

Choice depends on time elapsed, BMI, breastfeeding, preference; consider advance LNG prescription for high-risk patients (perimenopausal, irregular cycles, frequent missed pills).

cards.front: The first antenatal (booking) visit should ideally be before 10 weeks; it confirms pregnancy, establishes [___], and determines the model of care.
cards.context:
Early booking matters for two reasons: dating accuracy is highest before 14 weeks (CRL), and time-sensitive interventions start in T1 — folate continuation, smoking cessation, asymptomatic bacteriuria treatment.

Late booking (>14 weeks) misses these windows + forces less accurate later-pregnancy dating.

Rushing → missed teratogen or unrecognised mental health condition.

cards.front: Pregnancy tests confirm pregnancy by detecting the hormone beta-[___].
cards.context: Both urine and serum pregnancy tests detect beta-hCG, produced by the trophoblast soon after implantation. Serum quantitative levels also help track early-pregnancy viability and ectopic risk.

cards.front: Outpatient pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) empirical antibiotics: ceftriaxone (gonorrhoea) + [___] (chlamydia) + metronidazole (anaerobes).
cards.context:
PID is polymicrobial (Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Chlamydia trachomatis, Mycoplasma genitalium, anaerobes); empirical antibiotics must cover all: ceftriaxone (gonorrhoea) + doxycycline (chlamydia) + metronidazole (anaerobes).

Threshold to treat is deliberately low (CDC): any sexually active woman with pelvic pain + cervical motion tenderness OR uterine tenderness OR adnexal tenderness — start treatment.

Most managed as outpatients (oral, review at 72 h); admit for IV if pregnant, severe, suspected tubo-ovarian abscess, no response to oral, or unable to tolerate oral. Sexual partner notification + treatment essential.

cards.front: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome is perihepatitis causing RUQ pain — a complication of [___] (ascending genital-tract infection); classic finding is 'violin-string' adhesions at laparoscopy.
cards.context:
Fitz-Hugh-Curtis is perihepatitis from pelvic infection (classically chlamydia or gonorrhoea) tracking up the right paracolic gutter.

Laparoscopy is pathognomonic: 'violin-string' adhesions between liver capsule and anterior abdominal wall. Treat the underlying pelvic inflammatory disease (ceftriaxone + doxycycline + metronidazole).

cards.front: Couvelaire uterus is blood infiltration of the myometrium from severe placental abruption, causing uterine atony and PPH; risk of [___] from disrupted decidua.
cards.context:
Couvelaire uterus (uteroplacental apoplexy) is the visual signature of severe placental abruption at caesarean — blood has dissected from retroplacental haematoma into myometrium, producing a purple, bruised uterus.

Severe abruption also releases tissue factor + procoagulants from disrupted decidua → DIC (consumptive coagulopathy: falling platelets, falling fibrinogen, raised D-dimer, prolonged INR/APTT).

Hysterectomy may be unavoidable if uterotonics, B-Lynch, UAE all fail.

cards.front: Postnatal mood spectrum: baby blues peak at days [___] and self-resolve; postnatal depression peaks at 3-6 months. Screen with EPDS.
cards.context:
Postnatal mood disorders form a clinical spectrum and are separated by timing, severity and loss of reality testing.

Baby blues (70-80%, days 3-5, self-limiting tearfulness) — reassurance, support, monitoring.

Postnatal depression usually emerges later, often around 3-6 months, and is screened with the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS).

cards.front: The key bedside test in a jittery, poorly-feeding at-risk newborn is a blood [___].
cards.context:
Neonatal hypoglycaemia is often non-specific (jittery, poor feeding, lethargy, seizures).

So the at-risk baby (preterm, SGA/LGA, infant of a diabetic mother) needs a low threshold to check — the bedside glucose is the key test.

cards.front: MgSO₄ for fetal neuroprotection is given when imminent birth is anticipated before 30 weeks: 4 g IV loading dose, then [___] g/h infusion until birth or 24 h. The number-needed-to-treat to prevent one case of cerebral palsy is approximately 63.
cards.context:
MgSO₄ given antenatally for imminent preterm birth <30 weeks reduces cerebral palsy in survivors by ~30% (Cochrane). Mechanism is uncertain — possibly preventing glutamate excitotoxicity in the immature brain.

Regimen: 4 g IV loading over 20-30 min, then 1 g/h infusion for ≥4 h before delivery — aim as close to 4 h before birth as possible.

NNT ≈63: treat ~63 mothers to prevent one case of cerebral palsy. A modest absolute benefit, but cheap and low-risk, so given routinely at this gestation.

cards.front: The most common fracture sustained during birth is the [___].
cards.context: The commonest birth fracture, often after shoulder dystocia. Presents with reduced movement of the arm (pseudoparalysis), a palpable lump/crepitus, or an asymmetric Moro — and heals well with minimal intervention.

cards.front: APH is bleeding from the genital tract from 20+0 weeks until birth; affects [___]% of pregnancies; never perform digital VE until praevia excluded.
cards.context:
The 20-week threshold separates APH from threatened miscarriage; bleeding once labour has started is relabelled intrapartum haemorrhage.

Two safety rules drive the workup. First, stabilise the mother before chasing the cause: large-bore access, FBC + coag + group-and-hold, fetal assessment, and anti-D if Rh-negative.

Second, no digital vaginal exam until ultrasound has excluded placenta praevia — probing a low-lying placenta can provoke catastrophic haemorrhage.

cards.front: Small for gestational age (SGA) = estimated fetal weight (EFW) <10th centile; fetal growth restriction (FGR) is pathological, usually <3rd centile or abnormal [___].
cards.context:
The trap: SGA is a size label, FGR is a diagnosis of failed growth potential.

SGA just means EFW <10th centile. Many are constitutionally small but healthy (small parents, female fetus), needing only surveillance to confirm normal velocity with normal Dopplers.

FGR is the pathological subset, flagged by centile <3rd OR abnormal umbilical artery Dopplers signalling placental insufficiency. Doppler separates the at-risk fetus from the merely small one and drives delivery.

cards.front: USS signs of placenta accreta spectrum include loss of retroplacental clear zone, placental [___] (Swiss cheese), bladder wall interruption, and myometrial thinning.
cards.context:
Antenatal USS diagnosis of PAS — five signs of abnormal villous invasion: loss of retroplacental clear zone (sensitive, non-specific), placental lacunae ('Swiss cheese' — highest PPV in T2).

MRI is added for inconclusive USS or to map percreta extent (especially bladder/bowel invasion); USS sensitivity for PAS is ~80-90% in expert hands.

cards.front: Preterm birth is birth between 20+0 and [___]+6 weeks; affects ~8-9% of Australian pregnancies and is the leading cause of mortality in children <5.
cards.context:
Gestation is written weeks+days, so 20+0 = 20 weeks 0 days and 36+6 = the last day before 37 weeks (term); the 20-week floor is the same threshold that separates preterm birth from miscarriage.

Sub-categorised by severity: late preterm (34-36+6, ~70% of cases, generally good outcomes), moderate (32-33+6), very preterm (28-31+6, significant NICU need), and extremely preterm (<28 weeks).

Even late preterm infants have higher rates of learning difficulties, ADHD, and reduced educational attainment than term peers — which is why prevention matters even near term.
